primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes lysosomal globotriaosylceramide accumulation in vascular endothelium and multiple organs.
vignette: A young man has episodic burning pain in his hands and feet, angiokeratomas, hypohidrosis, and progressive kidney disease.
distractor_notes: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease.
key_expl: Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-galactosidase A deficiency.
objective: Identify the enzyme defect in Fabry disease.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes glucocerebroside accumulation in macrophages, leading to hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and bone disease.
vignette: A child has hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and recurrent bone pain. Marrow contains macrophages with crumpled tissue-paper cytoplasm.
distractor_notes: Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes Fabry disease.
Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy.
key_expl: Gaucher disease is caused by glucocerebrosidase deficiency.
objective: Identify the enzyme defect in Gaucher disease.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Hexosaminidase A deficiency prevents GM2 ganglioside degradation, causing progressive neurodegeneration without hepatosplenomegaly.
vignette: An infant has developmental regression, exaggerated startle, and a cherry-red macula without hepatosplenomegaly.
key_expl: Tay-Sachs disease results from GM2 ganglioside accumulation due to HEXA deficiency.
objective: Identify the stored substrate in Tay-Sachs disease.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency causes dermatan and heparan sulfate accumulation; unlike Hurler syndrome, corneal clouding is absent and inheritance is X-linked.
vignette: A boy has coarse facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, joint stiffness, developmental delay, and no corneal clouding.
lead: Which enzyme is deficient in this disorder?
distractor_notes: Alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency causes Hurler syndrome (MPS I), which commonly includes corneal clouding.
Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease.
Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes Fabry disease.
key_expl: Hunter syndrome is caused by iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency and is inherited in an X-linked pattern.
objective: Identify iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency in Hunter syndrome.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: ATP7B deficiency impairs biliary copper excretion and copper incorporation into ceruloplasmin, causing hepatic and neurologic copper accumulation.
vignette: A young adult has liver disease, tremor, psychiatric symptoms, low ceruloplasmin, and Kayser-Fleischer rings.
lead: Which organ normally provides the major route for excess copper excretion?
distractor_notes: Urinary copper rises in Wilson disease but biliary excretion is the normal major route.
Exhalation is not a major copper elimination pathway.
Pancreas does not excrete copper through insulin.
Sweat is not the principal route.
key_expl: ATP7B in hepatocytes transfers copper into bile for excretion.
objective: Identify biliary copper excretion as the key ATP7B-dependent process.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Inappropriately low hepcidin signaling increases ferroportin-mediated intestinal iron absorption and macrophage iron release, causing progressive tissue iron deposition.
vignette: A patient with HFE-related hereditary hemochromatosis has high transferrin saturation and systemic iron overload.
lead: Which regulatory hormone is functionally insufficient?
key_expl: Low hepcidin activity permits excessive ferroportin-mediated iron entry into plasma.
objective: Explain iron overload in hereditary hemochromatosis through hepcidin dysregulation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Trisomy 21 most often results from meiotic nondisjunction and is associated with intellectual disability, characteristic facial features, hypotonia, congenital heart disease, and increased leukemia/Alzheimer risk.
vignette: A newborn has hypotonia, upslanting palpebral fissures, single palmar crease, and an atrioventricular septal defect.
lead: Which chromosomal abnormality is most likely?
distractor_notes: Trisomy 18 causes Edwards syndrome with clenched fists and rocker-bottom feet.
key_expl: The phenotype and AV septal defect strongly support Down syndrome due to trisomy 21.
